workflowLabels: Real HTTP source editor mounts eleven modules and twenty-seven declared capabilities, including the required independent object authoring capability. Existing WebGL2 preview draws three authored UUIDs; the actual GPU implementation is recorded.

Adding a standard box reviews four objects and a fresh stable UUID. BOM, CRLF, original objects, camera and light are preserved. Chinese/English/Japanese at 390 px retain the same approval, name and UUID without horizontal overflow; Cancel writes neither source draft nor disk.

Reopening allocates a different add identity. Apply writes exactly the reviewed four-object candidate to memory only; ordinary Save persists its exact BOM/CRLF bytes and clears the editor dirty state.

Copy appends a fifth object with a fresh UUID and explicit same-source default name, preserving transforms and color. The separate transform form then changes only the copy’s position; ordinary Save leaves the original source object unchanged.

Removing the first stable UUID reviews a nullable after declaration and four survivors in unchanged source order. Ordinary Save and the existing readonly GPU preview reopen the resulting four-object scene.

Changing the actual raw source after approval and changing form intent without an input event each revoke Apply. Newer source bytes and the saved author file survive; no silent structural operation is authorized.
A real unsaved one-object author draft explicitly blocks removal of its last box. Cancel preserves that draft and the separate saved four-object source.

A legitimate object Apply does not bypass the ordinary disk Save precondition. External disk changes trigger the actual Save conflict dialog; Cancel preserves both the external file and the unsaved reviewed candidate.

With only WebGL2 explicitly injected as unavailable, the old readonly preview reports its renderer limit while native object review remains usable. Cancellation leaves author disk bytes intact. No rendering or backend authority enters the objects form.

Actual thirteen-module/twenty-nine-capability HTTP editor mounts the independent relative-translation author module. Native BOM/CRLF source contains escaped object keys and literal CRLF/Unicode names. No objects are preselected, offsets are zero, Check and Apply are disabled. The old readonly preview draws actual WebGL2 pixels with its software renderer explicitly recorded.

Two explicitly selected stable UUIDs, including one hidden by search, receive the same reviewed relative offset. Complete before/after objects and full candidate preserve every unselected object, nonposition field, BOM/CRLF and escaped-key spelling. Chinese/English/Japanese at 390px preserve filter, selection, inputs and approval, with one responsive comparison column and reachable controls. Cancel changes neither draft nor disk.

Apply accepts the exact advanced source-owner receipt and updates only unsaved source memory. Fresh readonly GPU preview visibly reflects the authored position change. Ordinary Save writes exactly the reviewed candidate; reopening the independent form reads those persisted positions and a second cancelled relative review starts from the new values.

Zero offset is a native unchanged result with no Apply approval. Explicit Select current results includes the boundary-position object; adding one metre would exceed its final bound, so the native operation rejects the whole batch while preserving raw offsets and all selections. No partial source/disk update occurs.

After review, silent checkbox, offset and query changes revoke the raw form signature. A newer source edit, with or without an input event, revokes the exact owned snapshot and cannot be overwritten by a previous candidate. Local inputs are retained for correction; none of these attempts applies or saves.

Actual portable browser modules preserve the private translation proposal brand. A serialized clone and cross-domain single-object transform apply reject it; this pure proof has no editor writer or Save port. Existing independent author modules remain mounted, while translation imports no sibling controller or renderer.

Legitimate translation still uses ordinary editor Save preconditions. A real external disk modification triggers the existing save-conflict dialog; Cancel preserves external bytes and the unsaved reviewed translation independently. The translation form never implicitly saves or writes metadata.

Explicit WebGL2-unavailable injection disables only drawing. The independent native relative-translation review remains available, alongside the existing author modules, with no renderer, World, execution or implicit Save dependency.

Real sixteen-module/thirty-two-capability HTTP editor mounts independent authored-axis even distribution. No objects are preselected; X is the sole default and there is no reference control. Fewer than three objects cannot enable Check or Apply. Native source includes BOM/CRLF, an escaped objects key and literal Unicode/CRLF names. Readonly preview draws actual WebGL2 pixels with software renderer recorded.

Three explicit stable UUIDs include two hidden rows. X distribution is ordered by original numeric coordinates; complete before/after stay in source declaration order. Endpoint objects and other fields retain their bytes; only the middle X component changes. Full source/BOM/CRLF/escaped spelling, three languages at 390px, native order, filter, axis, approval, responsive columns and reachable footer are asserted. Cancel changes neither draft nor disk.

Apply accepts the exact advanced owner receipt and updates unsaved memory only. A new readonly software-GPU preview reflects changed authored position. Ordinary Save writes the exact candidate; reopening reads persisted coordinates. Repeating the now-even distribution gives native no-op and no approval.

Y and Z distribution are separately reviewed, applied and saved with native numeric order and untouched endpoints. Equal-coordinate and signed-zero ties retain source order and negative-zero endpoint spelling. All-equal coordinates are a no-op. A one-ULP span unable to produce strictly increasing binary64 points is rejected atomically. A 128-object hidden-selection candidate reviews all declarations and monotonic positions, then Cancel leaves disk unchanged.

Silent checkbox, authored-axis or query mutations revoke approval. Source edits with or without input events cannot be overwritten by an old candidate. Detached closed-owner and old-query rows cannot change current global selection; normal rows work. No such attempt applies or saves.

The seventh private authoring proposal brand is retained by real portable browser modules. Serialized clones and cross-domain alignment application reject it. A two-object request is rejected at bridge cardinality admission with its exact request error. This pure proof has no writer/Save port and borrows no sibling or renderer authority.

A legitimate distributed draft still uses ordinary editor Save preconditions. External disk modification opens the existing conflict dialog; Cancel preserves external disk bytes and unsaved reviewed candidate independently. Distribution never implicitly saves or writes metadata.

Explicit WebGL2-unavailable injection affects drawing only. Independent native even-distribution review remains available alongside all sixteen modules, without renderer, World, backend or implicit Save authority.
Actual HTTP runtime mounts the independent eighth module and renders three shaded boxes through WebGL2; authored identities and exact source locations remain inspectable.
Real pointer orbit changes rendered pixels; reset restores the authored camera exactly without source, metadata or Save writes.
Unsaved source rotation changes the actual GPU image while author files retain their original saved bytes.
Invalid raw source reports native diagnostics and retains the previous valid GPU model; correcting and refreshing recovers without an implicit Save.
Actual ResizeObserver redraws bounded buffers at 390 px; Chinese, English and Japanese controls/inspector remain scrollable without horizontal overflow.
Closing loses the owned WebGL context. Ordinary editor Save preserves BOM/CRLF and stable object IDs, and reopening renders the persisted scene.
An explicitly injected unavailable-WebGL2 device shows verified declarations and a clear no-render fallback; the existing project/2D build entry stays mounted and saved author data is unchanged.

observations: Legacy single-object add/copy/remove desktop and English390 screenshots keep independent controls and ordinary-source review visible; identity/name fields fit the narrow dialog and actions wrap within the sticky footer.
Legacy batch translation desktop and Japanese390 screenshots retain explicit hidden-source selection, common XYZ offset and readable scrollable controls.
Legacy distribution desktop and Chinese390 screenshots retain authored-axis choice, global hidden selection and endpoint-order review with reachable footer.

Readonly preview desktop shows actual shaded boxes with selected edge emphasis and object identity inspector. Japanese390 image preserves author-camera Reset messaging, view controls and visible selection outline. Viewing these images does not establish hardware-GPU or author-write authority.

Only these eight legacy representative images plus the six previously recorded new-copy images were personally viewed; remaining seventeen produced images are not claimed as visually inspected. Full candidate/source correctness is established by each actual browser assertion rather than visual inspection of all scrollable text.

limits: Root exclusively ran all real HTTP/Chrome proofs in temporary author workspaces; this agent only read receipts and viewed files. The actual repository remains unapplied by the staged proof.
The four legacy workflows are compatibility checks on current sixteen-module/thirty-two-capability staging source and are not reuses of historical passing reports.

Objects producer tracks SVG requests but does not track CSP violations. Readonly preview tracks neither SVG requests nor CSP violations; missing observations are null with tracked:false, not fabricated zero.
All rendering is the recorded real Chrome/SwiftShader software WebGL implementation. No installed application, Android/device or hardware-GPU acceptance is claimed.
40 browser workflows represent different actual scopes. They are not added to UI/native/prepared/full-application totals as unique coverage. Existing summary and visual report remain unchanged.
